chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed this Quran, in it are beacons of guidance and lanterns for the darkness. So let a beholder brighten his sight and open his vision to the illumination, for indeed pondering is the revival of the heart of the insightful one, just as the enlightened one walks in the darkness with the light.

key_terms.التَّفَكُّرَ: Pondering/deep reflection — active contemplation that revives the heart
key_terms.حَيَاةُ قَلْبِ الْبَصِيرِ: Revival of the insightful heart — spiritual awakening through reflection
key_terms.مَصَابِيحُ الدُّجَى: Lanterns of darkness — lamps that dispel spiritual and intellectual darkness
key_terms.مَنَارُ الْهُدَى: Beacons/minarets of guidance — signposts that illuminate the path of truth

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the Quran as a source of guidance and light?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) extols the Quran as a source of guidance and light, urging believers to actively engage with it through deep reflection. The metaphor of the insightful person navigating darkness with a lamp illustrates how tafakkur (deep contemplation) illuminates the heart and enables spiritual perception. This teaching was addressed to a community that needed encouragement to move beyond passive recitation to active, transformative engagement with the Quran's meanings.
